headline: US CPI cools to 3.4%, easing Fed rate-hike pressure ahead of September meeting
tldr: US CPI fell to 3.4% in July, in line with forecasts, easing rate-hike fears and lifting stock futures and equities.
UK economy grew 0.4% in Q2, beating expectations, though Hormuz-driven inflation threatens to cloud Q3.
Clacton by-election polls open with Farage polling around 73%; a parliamentary standards probe resumes if he wins.
Power BI legacy browser upload path dies on 31 August — dashboards will silently show frozen data until that deadline.
FCA closed its premium finance market study with no cap but retains active monitoring under Consumer Duty.

sections.title: Markets
sections.body:
**Markets — Thursday 13 August 2026**

The swing factor flagged yesterday delivered: 
US CPI came in at 3.4% for July, slowing for a second consecutive month from 3.5% in June,
 and 
all readings were in line with Dow Jones consensus forecasts.
 No surprise means no fresh rate-hike panic. 
The print "possibly takes the urgency out of an imminent interest rate hike,"
 with the Fed not meeting again until September. 
The Iran-driven energy shock continues to fade at the margins — gasoline prices up 24.6% year-on-year, down from 26.7% in June.
 
Stock futures moved higher after the data, and Treasury yields pulled back broadly.



US stocks edged higher Wednesday: the S&P 500 gained 0.3%, the Nasdaq +0.5%, and the Dow closed just below flat
 — a CPI-relief rally capped by still-elevated oil. 
Brent crude hit $90 earlier in Wednesday's session, with WTI near $84.
 
Asian equity futures for Japan and South Korea advanced overnight
, consistent with IJPN's +1.66% in the pre-fetch. 
Nasdaq 100 contracts slipped slightly in Asian trading after Cisco's earnings disappointed.


In Europe, Wednesday was a pullback day. 
The FTSE 100 slipped 0.2% to 10,821, still the best performer among major European benchmarks, while Paris's CAC 40 shed 0.58%.
 
UK blue chips are caught between mixed earnings and opposing Bank of England rate signals.


**Sam's portfolio:** The defence tilt is paying off today. BAE +1.79%, Rolls-Royce +0.85%, and WDEF +1.49% all look geopolitical-premium driven — Hormuz remains shut with no resolution near. AMD's +1.82% and ASML's +0.59% follow the CPI relief trade in semis. IJPN's +1.66% reflects the broader Asia catch-up on the benign inflation read.

sections.title: Data & BI
sections.body:
**Data & BI**

Two items worth flagging today, both new since yesterday's briefing.

**Power BI — legacy "upload from browser" retirement hits hard deadline.** 
Microsoft is retiring the legacy browser-based Excel/CSV import in stages: existing semantic models built that way stopped refreshing on 31 July, and on **31 August** — this month — reports built on those legacy models will fail to open entirely.
 
Until then, dashboards will appear to work but numbers will be frozen as of the last successful refresh
 — the quiet failure mode that will catch people out. If anyone in your org built quick-and-dirty dashboards via the old Service upload path, 31 August is the hard stop.

**BigQuery — performance and DTS updates this week.** 
BigQuery has enhanced its vectorised execution using SIMD instructions, coupled with parallel algorithms applied at eligible query stages — Google claims up to 10× acceleration on qualifying queries and up to 40% overall slot time reduction.
 Separately, 
BigQuery Data Transfer Service (DTS) now supports direct ingestion into Apache Iceberg managed tables in preview, pulling from GCS, Amazon S3, and Azure Blob Storage.
 The Iceberg managed table support is the more structurally interesting one for teams running open lakehouse architectures.

The **PBIR default-on** item flagged yesterday remains unconfirmed as landed — worth checking your Desktop build version.

sections.title: Career & Data Leadership
sections.body:
**Salary benchmarks: where Head of Data sits right now**


[Bristow Holland](https://www.bristowholland.com/insights/industry-insights/uk-data-analytics-salary-expectations-in-2026-hiring-trends-and-workforce-planning/) puts Head of Data and data management leadership roles frequently above £90,000, particularly where the remit covers governance, reporting strategy, and enterprise data architecture.
 That aligns with the broader picture: 
[Digital Waffle](https://www.digitalwaffle.co/salary-guides) reports salaries rising 2–4% on average across UK tech, with stronger growth of up to 6% specifically in AI, data, and cybersecurity.
 
[Randstad Digital](https://www.randstaddigital.com/insights/blogs/managed-solutions/uk-salary-trends-2026-roles-skills-industries-highest-demand/) flags a distinct scarcity of digital expertise driving sharply rising and highly competitive salaries, particularly for leadership roles in AI, cloud, and data.


**The "data-driven" label is losing ground — deliberately**

A notable signal from Wavestone's Data and AI Leadership Survey, surfaced by [Kore1](https://www.kore1.com/data-team-org-chart-2026/): 
the share of companies willing to call themselves data-driven shrank back into the mid-30s, down from the mid-40s two years earlier — while the budgets they allocated to data and analytics kept growing.
 More candour, not less investment.

**The framing that gets data leaders fired**


[The Executive Outlook](https://theexecutiveoutlook.com/blogs/effective-data-leadership-tips-lead-drive-impact-2026) is blunt: in 2026, technical credibility alone is no longer sufficient — the executives driving real impact are those who lead the business *through* data, not just lead the data function.
 The practical test: 
presenting a churn model at 89% accuracy is providing information; presenting that the same model identified 340 at-risk accounts worth $4.2M in revenue, with a recommended intervention, is driving action.


**AI trust, not AI tooling, is now the blocker**

This moves the Hex finding from yesterday forward: 
[Hex's State of Data Teams survey](https://hex.tech/state-of-data-teams/) of 65+ data leaders found data quality and lack of trust (31%) as the top barrier to AI adoption — cited nearly twice as often as any other concern.
 For a Head of Data candidate, fixing the trust problem is now a more compelling interview narrative than deploying more tooling.

sections.title: UK Insurance
sections.body:
The motor losses and FCA rule simplification stories were covered in yesterday's briefing. The search results don't surface materially new developments on those fronts today. The most genuinely new items are: the FCA's live premium finance monitoring (post-market study conclusion), the FCA's AI governance shift, the home insurance weather-driven claims picture, and the Insurity/ITS partnership. Let me check if there's anything fresh on premium finance or home insurance specifically.
Nothing in today's search results signals a genuinely fresh breaking story from the last 24 hours on motor losses or FCA rule simplification — those were covered yesterday. The substantively new items not in yesterday's briefing are: the FCA premium finance final report outcome and its ongoing monitoring posture; the FCA's AI governance shift; the home insurance property claims/weather picture; and the Insurity/ITS tech partnership. Here's the section:

---

**FCA premium finance: no cap, but watch still on**


The FCA's February 2026 final report on the premium finance market study concluded with no sector-wide intervention.
 
Average APRs dropped from 23.3% in 2022 to 19.2% in 2026, saving consumers an estimated £157 million annually.
 The relief is qualified: 
the FCA has made clear its monitoring of the premium finance market does not end with this report, and it will continue to act under Consumer Duty where needed.
 
Fair Value Assessment concerns remain unresolved for some firms,
 so this is not a clean sign-off — it is a deferral of harder action contingent on conduct.


In 2024, 60% of motor policyholders and 41% of home policyholders who paid by instalments did so because they could not afford to pay annually,
 which makes this a vulnerability and access issue as much as a pricing one.

**AI: governance now the FCA's test, not adoption**


The FCA's focus on proving good customer outcomes is shifting insurers' AI priorities from adoption to governance.
 Firms that have been building AI tooling should expect supervisory attention to shift to whether those tools can be audited against outcome metrics — not just whether they exist.

**Home insurance: weather driving claims base**


Insurers paid out a record £4.6bn in property claims in the first three quarters of 2025, driven largely by severe weather, with extreme weather now treated as structural rather than exceptional.
 
In home insurance, that is translating into sharper differentiation by postcode and risk, alongside more emphasis on prevention and resilience.

**Events — diary these**

- **📅 4 Aug** — [Code for Her](https://protospace.uk/events) coding academy and forum for women, Aiimi HQ, 18:30–20:30. *(Past — for reference if you missed it.)*
- **📅 27 Aug** — [MKFM's Meet of MK End of Summer Party](https://allevents.in/milton-keynes/meetups), Hotel La Tour, from 17:00. Broad professional crowd; good for casual relationship-building.
- **📅 10 Sep** — [MKC TV × Work Café Santander](https://allevents.in/milton-keynes/meetups), Unity Place, 17:30. Media/business mixer — worth a look given Unity Place's growing role as MK's innovation anchor.
- **📅 16–18 Sep** — [TNMOC/London Mathematical Society Conference](https://protospace.uk/events), Bletchley Park. Niche but strong on data and computing history.
- **📅 12–16 Oct** — **MK Tech Week 2026.** 
The week runs 12–16 October, culminating in a one-day conference and expo at Unity Place on 15 October focused on sovereign technology — how the UK develops and protects critical tech, data and digital infrastructure.
 
Partners confirmed include The Open University, MK:U, MK College Group, HMGCC, BSI, Serve Robotics, and Bletchley Park.
 Programme is live at [miltonkeynestechweek.com](https://miltonkeynestechweek.com).

**Local news**

**MK Tech Week theme confirmed.** The sovereign technology framing is new detail since yesterday. 
The conference will focus on the UK's ability to develop, secure and control critical technologies, data and digital infrastructure that underpin economic resilience and national security.
 Directly relevant territory for a senior data professional — worth monitoring the speaker programme as it builds.

**Council housing review open.** 
MKCC is reviewing its Housing Revenue Account Business Plan and wants tenants to help shape future priorities; the consultation closes 6 September 2026.
 Low priority for Sam directly, but signals where council attention and capital are going this autumn.

sections.title: News
sections.body:
**UK GDP — better than feared.** The ONS Q2 figures, out this morning, show the economy grew 0.4% between April and June. 
[GB News](https://www.gbnews.com/politics/clacton-by-election-latest-nigel-farage-count-binface-essex-parliament-westminster) reports growth of 0.4% for the quarter, following a contraction of 0.1% in April and modest 0.1% recovery in May, with June's 0.3% jump — driven partly by pre-conflict oil-price uncertainty — doing the heavy lifting.
 That comfortably beats the OBR's implied quarterly run-rate and gives the Burnham government a rare piece of good news. 
[FXStreet](https://www.fxstreet.com/news/uk-gdp-expected-to-show-moderate-q2-growth-202608130200) notes that Strait of Hormuz tensions mean inflationary pressure is likely to build from July, clouding the Q3 outlook.


**Clacton polls open.** 
[GB News](https://www.gbnews.com/politics/clacton-by-election-latest-nigel-farage-count-binface-essex-parliament-westminster) reports up to 75,000 voters are expected to turn out today, with Farage — who resigned his seat to trigger the contest in what he called a "people vs establishment" vote — standing again.
 
[PollCheck](https://www.pollcheck.co.uk/by-elections/clacton) shows a Survation poll putting Farage on around 73%, with satirical candidate Count Binface second on about 20%.
 
[GB News](https://www.gbnews.com/politics/clacton-by-election-latest-nigel-farage-count-binface-essex-parliament-westminster) notes the parliamentary standards investigation into a £5m gift he received will resume if he wins.
 Result expected overnight.

**Turkey–Kurdistan amnesty.** 
[NPR/AP](https://www.npr.org/sections/world/) reports Turkey's parliament approved legislation introducing a conditional pardon for thousands of Kurdish militants, part of the government's peace initiative with the insurgent group.
 A significant shift after four decades of conflict, though implementation will be closely watched.

**Russia releases American detainee.** 
[NPR](https://www.npr.org/sections/world/) reports Russia released an American military veteran yesterday, allowing his return to the US after four years of what his family and officials allege was wrongful incarceration and abusive treatment.
